fields.name: goal_target
fields.description: The single target position, in [y, x], on which the goal-named cube (the colour named in the goal instruction) is to be dropped. Written at step #1, the only step that shows the demonstration, and copied unchanged at every later step; unknown before the demonstration has been seen. Fill it by this procedure and no other: (1) walk the demonstration frames in ascending t. (2) A placement is a frame where the gripper is low (height below ~0.07) and the fingers go from a partly closed value (anything between ~45% and ~95%; the low frame itself may read 67%, 80% or 93%) to ~100% open, in the frames right after the goal-named cube was carried (its line read 'held in the gripper' while the gripper was raised). (3) The placement's target is the listed target closest to where the cube then rests, with its coordinates copied from the last demonstration frame, where all four targets are listed. (4) Discard the final placement of the demonstration, the one that leaves the cube near [82, 127] with no target within ~15 pixels; discard button presses (fingers 0%, no cube carried); ignore a carried cube that momentarily loses its 'held' label while the gripper stays raised. (5) Number the remaining placements 1, 2, 3, 4 in the order they occur, earliest = 1, and write the target of the placement whose number the goal's ordinal names ('first' = 1, 'second' = 2, 'third' = 3, 'fourth' = 4). The ordinal always counts forward from the earliest placement, never backward from the most recent one, and a button press between placements does not restart the count. Example: placements in order onto targets near [99, 90], [100, 163], [141, 133], [79, 90], then the centre set-down; goal 'second' gives the last-frame listing of the second one, e.g. [98, 166]; goal 'first' gives [99, 90]. e.g. [139, 124]
